[Payroll & Compensation](https://salarybox.in/blog/category/payroll-compensation/)


# What Is the Minimum Number of Employees Required for PF, ESI, Gratuity, and Bonus in India?


October 12, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/what-is-the-minimum-number-of-employees-required-for-pf-esi-gratuity-and-bonus-in-india/#respond)


Every Indian business owner hits the same wall at some point: “We just hired our 10th person. Do we need to register for ESI now? What about PF? When does gratuity kick in?”


These are not abstract questions. Getting the threshold wrong can cost you lakhs in penalties, interest charges, and even imprisonment under certain labour laws. And the rules are not the same across all laws. PF kicks in at 20 employees. ESI can apply at 10 in factories. Gratuity starts at 10 employees but has completely different eligibility rules.


The problem is that no single government website consolidates all these thresholds in one place. Business owners have to read through the EPF Act, ESI Act, Payment of Gratuity Act, and Payment of Bonus Act separately, and then figure out how state level laws like Professional Tax and Labour Welfare Fund layer on top.


This guide puts every applicability threshold, wage limit, contribution rate, and registration deadline in one place so you know exactly when each law applies to your business.


## Quick Reference: Master Applicability Threshold Table


Before diving into the details, here is the complete picture at a glance.


Labour Law Minimum Employees Wage/Salary Limit Employer Contribution Employee Contribution


EPF (Provident Fund) 20 Basic + DA up to ₹15,000/month 12% of basic + DA 12% of basic + DA


ESI (Employee State Insurance) 10 (factory) / 20 (others) Gross up to ₹21,000/month 3.25% 0.75%


Gratuity 10 No wage limit 4.81% of basic (approx.) Nil


Bonus 20 Salary up to ₹21,000/month 8.33% to 20% Nil


Professional Tax 1 (varies by state) Varies by state Nil Up to ₹2,500/year


Maternity Benefit 10 No wage limit As per Act Nil (covered by employer/ESI)


Minimum Wages 1 Scheduled employment As per notification N/A


Shops & Establishments 1 No limit N/A N/A


Labour Welfare Fund Varies by state Varies ₹20 to ₹75/year ₹6 to ₹52/year


Now let us break down each law in detail.


## 1. Provident Fund (EPF): 20 or More Employees


The Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 is the most common compliance trigger for growing businesses.


### When Does PF Apply?


PF becomes mandatory when your establishment employs **20 or more persons** on any day. This includes all types of workers: permanent, temporary, contractual, and casual employees.


PF Applicability Factor Details


Minimum employees 20 on any single day


Types of employees counted All categories: permanent, temporary, contract, casual


Wage ceiling for contribution ₹15,000/month (basic + DA)


Employee contribution 12% of basic + DA


Employer contribution 12% of basic + DA (3.67% to EPF + 8.33% to EPS)


Registration deadline Within one month of crossing the threshold


Voluntary registration Available for establishments with fewer than 20 employees


### The “Once Covered, Always Covered” Rule


This is one of the most critical rules that business owners miss. Once your establishment becomes covered under the EPF Act (because you had 20 or more employees), the Act continues to apply even if your employee count drops below 20 later. You cannot deregister simply because you reduced staff.


For example, if your Pune based IT services company had 22 employees in March 2026 and you registered for PF, but then 5 employees resigned in April bringing the count to 17, you still need to continue PF compliance for all remaining employees.


### Voluntary PF Registration


If you have fewer than 20 employees, you can still register voluntarily. This requires consent from the employer and a majority of employees. Many startups choose voluntary registration because it helps attract talent. Employees see PF as a basic benefit, and companies offering it from day one appear more professional.


To understand[how EPF contributions are calculated](https://salarybox.in/blog/epf-contributions-calculated-guide-employees/) and the recent[EPF reforms](https://salarybox.in/blog/employee-provident-fund-epf-reforms/) that affect contribution rates, check our detailed guides.


### PF Contribution Breakdown


Component Employee Share Employer Share


EPF (Provident Fund) 12% 3.67%


EPS (Pension Scheme) Nil 8.33%


EDLI (Insurance) Nil 0.50%


Admin charges Nil 0.50%


**Total** **12%** **13%**


Note: The contribution is calculated on basic salary plus dearness allowance. If an employee’s basic + DA is ₹20,000 per month, the contribution is still calculated on ₹15,000 (the wage ceiling) unless the employer opts to contribute on the actual salary.


### What Counts as an “Establishment” for PF?


The EPF Act applies to every establishment that is a factory engaged in any industry listed in Schedule 1 of the Act, and to any other establishment employing 20 or more persons. This covers factories, shops, offices, and virtually every type of business.


## 2. ESI (Employee State Insurance): 10 or 20 Employees


The Employees’ State Insurance Act, 1948 provides medical, sickness, maternity, and disablement benefits to employees.


### When Does ESI Apply?


The threshold depends on the type of establishment:


Establishment Type Minimum Employees for ESI


Factories (using power) 10 or more


Factories (without power) 20 or more


Shops, hotels, restaurants, cinemas, road transport, newspaper establishments 20 or more (10 in some states)


Medical and educational institutions 20 or more (where notified)


Private IT/ITES establishments As notified by state government


### ESI Wage Limit


ESI applies only to employees earning a gross salary of **₹21,000 per month or less** (₹25,000 for persons with disability). If an employee’s gross salary exceeds ₹21,000, that individual employee is exempt from ESI, but the establishment must still be registered if it meets the employee count threshold.


ESI Factor Details


Employee wage ceiling ₹21,000/month gross (₹25,000 for PwD)


Employer contribution 3.25% of gross wages


Employee contribution 0.75% of gross wages


Total contribution 4% of gross wages


Contribution period 1 April to September


Contribution period 2 October to March


Payment due date 15th of the following month


### Important: State Notifications Matter


Several state governments have notified ESI applicability for establishments with 10 or more employees, even for non-factory establishments. Before assuming the 20 employee threshold applies to your business, check the notification issued by your state government.


For instance, the ESI Corporation has been progressively expanding coverage to new areas and types of establishments. If your business operates in a recently notified area, you may need to register even if you were previously exempt.


For a complete understanding of how ESI fits into your[payroll compliance checklist](https://salarybox.in/blog/payroll-compliance-checklist-for-indian-smes-2025-update/) , including deadlines and filing requirements, refer to our detailed compliance guide.


### How ESI and PF Interact


Many business owners ask whether they need both ESI and PF. The answer is: it depends on your employee count and their salaries.


Scenario PF Applicable? ESI Applicable?


8 employees, all earning ₹18,000/month No (below 20) No (below 10/20 threshold)


12 employees in a factory, earning ₹15,000/month No (below 20 for PF) Yes (10+ in factory for ESI)


22 employees, all earning ₹35,000/month Yes (20+ for PF) Registered, but no ESI deduction (salary above ₹21,000)


25 employees, 15 earning ₹18,000 and 10 earning ₹30,000 Yes (20+) Yes for 15 employees earning below ₹21,000


## 3. Gratuity: 10 or More Employees


The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 applies to establishments employing 10 or more persons on any day in the preceding 12 months.


### When Does Gratuity Apply?


Gratuity Applicability Factor Details


Minimum employees 10 on any day in the preceding 12 months


Employee eligibility 5 years of continuous service


Calculation formula Last drawn salary × 15/26 × years of service


Maximum gratuity payable ₹20,00,000


“Once covered, always covered” Yes, continues even if employees drop below 10


Applicable to Factories, mines, oilfields, plantations, ports, railway companies, shops, and establishments


### Understanding the “Any Day in Preceding 12 Months” Rule


This is where many employers get confused. You do not need to maintain 10 employees throughout the year. If on even a single day in the past 12 months you had 10 or more employees (including temporary and contract workers), the Gratuity Act applies to your establishment.


For example, suppose your retail business in Hyderabad normally has 7 full time employees. During Diwali season (October to November), you hire 4 temporary workers, bringing the total to 11. The Gratuity Act now applies to your establishment, and it continues to apply even after the temporary workers leave.


### Gratuity Calculation with Example


For an employee who has worked for 8 years and 7 months (rounds up to 9 years since the service period exceeds 6 months in the last year) with a last drawn monthly salary (basic + DA) of ₹25,000:


**Gratuity = ₹25,000 × 15/26 × 9 = ₹1,29,808**


Component Value


Last drawn salary (basic + DA) ₹25,000/month


Service period 8 years 7 months (rounded to 9 years)


Calculation ₹25,000 × 15 ÷ 26 × 9


Gratuity amount ₹1,29,808


For a detailed breakdown of how[gratuity works as an employee benefit](https://salarybox.in/blog/understanding-gratuity-a-powerful-tool-for-motivating-and-engaging-employees/) , including tax implications and special cases, read our comprehensive guide.


### Key Point: No Wage Ceiling for Gratuity


Unlike PF and ESI, there is no wage ceiling for gratuity applicability. Every employee who has completed 5 years of continuous service is eligible, regardless of their salary level. The only cap is on the maximum gratuity payable, which is ₹20 lakh.


## 4. Bonus: 20 or More Employees


The Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 mandates that employers pay a bonus to eligible employees.


### When Does the Bonus Act Apply?


Bonus Applicability Factor Details


Minimum employees 20 or more on any day during the accounting year


Employee salary eligibility Up to ₹21,000/month


Calculation ceiling ₹7,000/month or minimum wage (whichever is higher)


Minimum bonus 8.33% of salary


Maximum bonus 20% of salary


Payment deadline Within 8 months of closing the accounting year


“Once covered, always covered” Yes


New establishments Exempt for first 5 years (with conditions)


### Who Gets Bonus and How Much?


Not every employee in a covered establishment is eligible for bonus. The Act specifies these conditions:


Condition Requirement


Minimum working days 30 days in the accounting year


Salary threshold Drawing up to ₹21,000/month


Disqualification Dismissed for fraud, violent behaviour, or theft


The minimum bonus of 8.33% is payable regardless of whether the company made a profit. This is often referred to as “statutory bonus.” If the company has allocable surplus, it may need to pay up to 20%.


### Bonus Calculation Example


For an employee earning ₹18,000 per month:


Since the salary (₹18,000) exceeds the calculation ceiling (₹7,000 or minimum wage, whichever is higher), the bonus is calculated on the ceiling amount.


Assuming the applicable minimum wage is ₹8,500 per month (higher than ₹7,000):


**Minimum bonus = ₹8,500 × 12 × 8.33% = ₹8,497 per year**


**Maximum bonus = ₹8,500 × 12 × 20% = ₹20,400 per year**


### New Establishment Exemption


If your business is newly established, you get a conditional exemption for the first 5 years. During this period, bonus is payable only in the years where you have made a profit. However, starting from the 6th year, the minimum bonus of 8.33% is mandatory regardless of profitability.


## 5. Other Labour Laws and Their Thresholds


Beyond the four major laws, several other regulations kick in at specific employee counts. Understanding these is equally important for full compliance.


### Maternity Benefit Act, 1961


Factor Details


Applicability 10 or more employees


Benefit duration 26 weeks paid leave (first 2 children), 12 weeks (third child onwards)


Eligibility 80 days of work in 12 months preceding delivery


Work from home Employer may allow after 26 weeks, if nature of work permits


Crèche facility Mandatory for establishments with 50+ employees


Interaction with ESI If ESI covers the employee, maternity benefit is provided through ESI


### Shops and Establishments Act


This is a state level law, and every state has its own version. The key point is that it applies to virtually every business, even with just 1 employee.


State Registration Threshold Registration Deadline


Maharashtra All shops and commercial establishments Within 30 days of commencing business


Karnataka All shops and establishments Within 30 days


Delhi All commercial establishments Within 30 days


Tamil Nadu All shops and establishments Within 30 days


Gujarat All shops and establishments Within 30 days of commencing work


This means even a solo founder who hires their first employee needs to register under the Shops and Establishments Act of their state.


### Professional Tax


[Professional Tax](https://salarybox.in/blog/understanding-indian-payroll-tax-structure/) is a state level tax that applies to salaried individuals and professionals. Not all states levy it, and rates vary significantly.


State Maximum Annual PT Monthly Deduction Range


Maharashtra ₹2,500 ₹175 to ₹300/month


Karnataka ₹2,400 ₹200/month


West Bengal ₹2,500 ₹110 to ₹208/month


Andhra Pradesh ₹2,500 ₹150 to ₹200/month


Telangana ₹2,500 ₹150 to ₹200/month


Tamil Nadu ₹2,500 ₹135 to ₹208/month


Gujarat ₹2,500 ₹200/month


Madhya Pradesh ₹2,500 ₹150 to ₹208/month


States that do not levy Professional Tax include Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttarakhand, Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and several northeastern states.


### Labour Welfare Fund (LWF)


LWF is a state level fund, and both the contribution amount and frequency vary by state.


State Employee Contribution Employer Contribution Frequency


Maharashtra ₹6/half year ₹18/half year Half yearly (June & December)


Karnataka ₹20/year ₹40/year Annual (January)


Tamil Nadu ₹10/half year ₹20/half year Half yearly


Delhi ₹0.75/month ₹0.75/month Half yearly


Andhra Pradesh ₹30/year ₹70/year Annual


Gujarat ₹6/half year ₹12/half year Half yearly


### Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970


Factor Details


Applicability for principal employer 20 or more contract workers on any day in the preceding 12 months


Applicability for contractor 20 or more workers on any day in the preceding 12 months


Registration Principal employer must register; contractor must obtain a licence


## The Complete Threshold Map: When Each Law Kicks In


This section gives you a clear picture of what happens as your business grows from 1 employee to 50 and beyond.


### Growth Stage: 1 to 9 Employees


Law Status


Shops & Establishments Act Applicable (register within 30 days)


Minimum Wages Act Applicable (pay at least the state minimum wage)


Professional Tax Applicable (in states that levy it)


TDS on Salary Applicable if salary exceeds basic exemption limit


PF Not mandatory (voluntary registration available)


ESI Not mandatory


Gratuity Not applicable yet


Bonus Not applicable


Maternity Benefit Not applicable


### Growth Stage: 10 to 19 Employees


Law Status


Everything from Stage 1 Still applicable


ESI Mandatory if it is a factory (10+ threshold)


Gratuity Now applicable (10+ threshold)


Maternity Benefit Act Now applicable (10+ threshold)


PF Still not mandatory (but voluntary registration available)


Bonus Still not applicable


### Growth Stage: 20 to 49 Employees


Law Status


Everything from Stage 1 and 2 Still applicable


PF Now mandatory (20+ threshold)


ESI Now mandatory for non-factory establishments (20+ threshold)


Bonus Now applicable (20+ threshold)


Contract Labour Act Applicable if you use 20+ contract workers


### Growth Stage: 50+ Employees


Law Status


Everything from previous stages Still applicable


Crèche facility Mandatory under Maternity Benefit Act


Industrial Disputes Act Specific provisions on layoffs, retrenchment, and closure apply at 100+


Internal Complaints Committee Mandatory under POSH Act (10+ employees)


## How to Check Which Laws Apply to Your Business


Follow this step by step process to determine your compliance requirements:


**Step 1: Count your total employees correctly**


Include every person who works for your business: full time, part time, temporary, contract, and casual workers. Do not exclude anyone based on their designation or salary level when counting for threshold purposes.


**Step 2: Identify your establishment type**


Determine whether your business is classified as a factory, shop, or commercial establishment. This affects the ESI threshold (10 for factories versus 20 for others).


**Step 3: Check the wage and salary levels**


Even if your establishment crosses the employee threshold, individual employees may be exempt from certain laws based on their salary. For example, employees earning above ₹21,000 gross are exempt from ESI contribution, and employees earning above ₹21,000 per month are exempt from the Bonus Act.


**Step 4: Verify state specific requirements**


Check your state’s Shops and Establishments Act, Professional Tax rules, and Labour Welfare Fund requirements. These vary significantly across states. If your business operates in[multiple states](https://salarybox.in/best-hrms-software-for-multi-state-expansion-in-india-2026-compliance-features-and-scalable-solutions/) , you need to comply with each state’s rules separately.


**Step 5: Register within the prescribed timeline**


Law Registration Deadline


EPF Within 1 month of crossing 20 employees


ESI Within 15 days of becoming applicable


Shops & Establishments Within 30 days of starting business


Professional Tax Within 30 days of becoming liable


## Penalties for Not Registering on Time


Missing the registration deadline does not make the law inapplicable. You will owe contributions from the date the law became applicable, plus interest and penalties.


Law Penalty for Non Registration


EPF Up to ₹5,000 fine + 1 year imprisonment + 1% per month damages on delayed contributions


ESI Up to ₹5,000 fine + 12% annual interest on delayed contributions


Gratuity Up to ₹10,000 fine + 1 year imprisonment + ₹1,000/day for continuing offence


Bonus Up to ₹1,000 fine + 6 months imprisonment


Shops & Establishments ₹1,000 to ₹25,000 depending on state

## Code on Social Security, 2020: What Changes Are Coming


The Code on Social Security, 2020 consolidates 9 existing laws (including the EPF Act, ESI Act, Payment of Gratuity Act, and Payment of Bonus Act) into a single code. Here is what may change when the rules under this code are fully notified:


Current Law Current Threshold Expected Under New Code


EPF 20 employees Government may notify a lower threshold


ESI 10/20 employees May be extended to all establishments with 10+ employees


Gratuity 10 employees May be reduced to cover gig and platform workers


Bonus 20 employees Threshold likely to remain at 20


The Code also introduces coverage for gig workers, platform workers, and self-employed individuals, which is a significant expansion from the current framework. However, until the rules are fully notified and enforced, the existing thresholds under individual Acts remain applicable.


Keep track of[recent changes in Indian payroll laws](https://salarybox.in/blog/recent-changes-in-indian-payroll-laws/) to stay updated as these transitions happen.

## Common Mistakes Businesses Make


### Mistake 1: Not Counting Contract Workers


Many businesses believe that contract workers or outsourced staff do not count toward the threshold. This is incorrect. For PF, ESI, and the Contract Labour Act, contract workers employed through a contractor at your premises are counted when determining applicability.


### Mistake 2: Thinking Salary Exempts the Establishment


If all your employees earn above ₹21,000 per month, you still need to register for ESI if you meet the employee count threshold. No ESI deductions will be made from their salary, but the registration requirement remains.


### Mistake 3: Not Provisioning for Gratuity from Day One


Many[small businesses](https://salarybox.in/best-hr-software-for-small-businesses-in-india-2025-top-picks-features-and-pricing-guide/) do not set aside gratuity provisions until an employee actually completes 5 years and claims it. This leads to a sudden, large payout that strains cash flow. The correct approach is to provision 4.81% of basic salary every month from the time the Gratuity Act becomes applicable.


### Mistake 4: Ignoring the “Once Covered, Always Covered” Rule


As discussed earlier, once PF, Gratuity, or the Bonus Act becomes applicable to your establishment, it continues to apply even if your employee count drops below the threshold. Some businesses try to deregister after reducing staff, but this is not legally permitted and can result in penalties.


### Mistake 5: Not Registering for Multiple State Compliances


If your business operates across multiple states, you need separate registrations for Professional Tax, Labour Welfare Fund, and Shops & Establishments in each state. ## Frequently Asked Questions


### 1. Can an employer with fewer than 20 employees voluntarily register for PF?


Yes. Under Section 1(4) of the EPF Act, an employer and the majority of employees can jointly apply to the Central Provident Fund Commissioner for voluntary coverage. Once granted, the establishment becomes covered under the EPF Act with the same rights and obligations as mandatorily covered establishments. Many[startups](https://salarybox.in/hrms-software-for-startups-in-india-quick-setup-in-under-24-hours-for-seamless-payroll-and-attendance-management/) opt for voluntary registration to offer PF benefits and attract better talent.


### 2. Do contract workers count toward the employee threshold for PF and ESI?


For PF, the count of 20 employees includes all categories of workers, including contract workers engaged through a contractor. For ESI, the threshold count includes employees directly employed by the establishment. Contract workers are covered under their contractor’s ESI registration. However, the principal employer has the ultimate responsibility to ensure compliance.


### 3. What happens if an employee’s salary crosses ₹21,000 after ESI registration?


If an employee who was contributing to ESI receives a salary increase that takes their gross above ₹21,000, they continue to receive ESI benefits until the end of the current contribution period (either September or March). From the next contribution period, they become exempt from ESI contribution. The establishment itself remains registered as long as it meets the employee count threshold.


### 4. Is gratuity applicable to employees who resign before completing 5 years?


Generally, no. An employee must complete 5 years of continuous service to be eligible for gratuity. However, there are exceptions. Gratuity is payable regardless of the service period in the event of death or disablement of the employee. Some court rulings have also held that a service period of 4 years and 240 days can be treated as 5 years for gratuity purposes.


### 5. Can a startup claim exemption from the Bonus Act for the first 5 years?


Yes, under Section 16 of the Payment of Bonus Act, a new establishment is not required to pay minimum bonus during the first 5 years. However, bonus is payable in any profitable year during this period, calculated based on the allocable surplus. From the 6th year onward, the minimum bonus of 8.33% is mandatory regardless of profitability.


### 6. How do I determine whether my establishment is a “factory” for ESI purposes?


Under the Factories Act, 1948, a “factory” is a premises where 10 or more workers work (or worked on any day in the preceding 12 months) with the aid of power, or 20 or more workers work without the aid of power, in a manufacturing process. If your establishment meets this definition, the lower ESI threshold of 10 employees applies. Most IT companies, consulting firms, and service businesses are not factories and follow the 20 employee threshold.


### 7. Does the Maternity Benefit Act apply even if the establishment is covered under ESI?


If an establishment is covered under ESI and the female employee is eligible for ESI benefits (earning up to ₹21,000 gross), the maternity benefit is provided through the ESI scheme. The employer does not need to separately comply with the Maternity Benefit Act for that employee. However, for female employees earning above ₹21,000 (who are not covered under ESI), the employer must provide maternity benefits directly under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961.


### 8. What are the penalties for not paying gratuity on time?


Under Section 9 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, the employer must pay gratuity within 30 days of it becoming payable (from the date it becomes due). If the employer does not pay within this period, the employer is liable to pay simple interest at a rate notified by the government (currently 10% per annum) from the date of the employee’s application. Additionally, non-payment can result in a fine of up to ₹10,000, imprisonment of up to 1 year, or both. For a continuing offence, an additional penalty of ₹1,000 per day can be imposed.
